title: Procedural lighthouse
prompt: Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. Model a coastal lighthouse entirely from code (no external model, texture or image files). It must read clearly as a lighthouse: a tapered tower with alternating painted bands (at least 3 bands in two contrasting colours), a gallery balcony with a railing near the top, a glass lantern room with a visible lamp, a conical or domed roof with a finial, a door and at least 4 small windows spiralling or stacked up the tower, and a rocky base made of several irregular rocks sitting on a patch of sea or ground. Add a small keeper's cottage next to the base. The camera must frame the whole lighthouse with some sky/horizon visible and slowly orbit it. Use lighting that gives clear form (a key light with shadows plus fill). When the first frame has rendered, set window.__TASK_STATE__ = { ready: true, partCount: <number of distinct visible mesh parts you created>, bandCount: <number of tower bands> }.
functionalChecklist: Page is a vite app with a canvas #app that renders a non-blank 3D frame with no console errors
Source builds the tower from tapered geometry (cone frustum, lathe, or scaled stacked segments) rather than a single cylinder
At least 3 tower bands with at least 2 distinct colours are defined in source
A gallery with railing (multiple posts or a ring) is present near the top
A lantern room with an emissive or bright lamp element and a roof with finial is present
At least 4 windows and one door are created
At least 5 rock pieces with varied scale/rotation form the base, and a cottage exists
window.__TASK_STATE__ is set after first render with ready === true, partCount >= 30 and bandCount >= 3
No external asset files are fetched (network requests only for the app's own bundle)
Camera orbits slowly: frames captured 2 seconds apart differ
visualRubric: A strong frame shows the whole lighthouse centred, readable at thumbnail size. Score each 1-5: (1) Silhouette and proportion: tapered tower, gallery, lantern and roof read unmistakably as a lighthouse, with a cottage and rocks in believable scale. (2) Detail density: railing, windows, door, bands, finial, trim rings, rock variety are all visible rather than a stack of plain cylinders. (3) Materials and colour: banding is crisp, lamp glows, stone/roof/glass look distinct, palette is coherent. (4) Lighting and depth: shadows, shading gradients and fill give volume, sea or ground and sky give context, nothing is flat or blown out. (5) Composition and polish: framing leaves margins, no z-fighting, floating parts or clipping, horizon is level.
probe: Load the page, wait until window.__TASK_STATE__.ready === true (timeout 20s), read partCount and bandCount, and capture frames at t=1s and t=3s. Pass the motion check if mean per-pixel absolute difference between the two frames exceeds a small threshold (e.g. 0.5% of pixels changed by more than 8/255). Also confirm the canvas #app is non-uniform (colour variance above threshold) and there are no uncaught page errors.

title: Procedural medieval handcart
prompt: Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. Model a medieval wooden hand-cart entirely from code (no external model, texture or image files). It must include: a plank-built open box bed (at least 8 individual planks or boards, with slight variation in length, tone or tilt), two large spoked wooden wheels (each with a hub, a rim and at least 8 spokes) on a shared axle, two long push handles at the rear, a front support leg or prop stand, corner posts with at least 2 cross rails per side, and iron-coloured fittings (bands on the hubs, bolts or straps). Load the cart with a few props: at least 3 sacks or barrels and a couple of crates, placed convincingly. Place the cart on a simple dirt ground with a few scattered stones. Show it from a three-quarter view and rotate the wheels slowly in place, or turntable the whole cart, so it reads in 3D. Use warm natural lighting with soft shadows. After the first frame set window.__TASK_STATE__ = { ready: true, wheelCount: <wheels>, spokeCount: <total spokes>, plankCount: <planks in the bed> }.
functionalChecklist: Page is a vite app with canvas #app rendering a non-blank 3D frame with no console errors
Two wheels, each built from hub, rim and at least 8 spokes (total spokes >= 16)
Cart bed has at least 8 planks with per-plank variation (position, scale, colour or rotation) in source
Axle connects both wheels at consistent positions and the wheels are on opposite sides of the bed
Two push handles and a front support leg exist
At least 2 distinct iron-coloured fitting elements (hub bands, bolts or straps) are present
At least 3 sacks/barrels and 2 crates are placed as cargo, plus ground with scattered stones
window.__TASK_STATE__ is set after first render with ready === true, wheelCount === 2, spokeCount >= 16, plankCount >= 8
No external asset files are fetched
Motion exists: frames captured 2 seconds apart differ (wheel spin or turntable)
visualRubric: A strong frame shows the whole cart at three-quarter angle with wheels clearly circular and spoked. Score each 1-5: (1) Structural plausibility: wheels touch the ground, axle aligns, bed sits on it, handles and prop leg make mechanical sense. (2) Craft detail: individual planks, spokes, rails, iron bands and bolts are visible; wood looks assembled not extruded. (3) Material and colour: wood tones vary, iron reads darker and metallic, sacks/barrels differ from the cart, palette is warm and cohesive. (4) Lighting and grounding: soft shadows under the cart and cargo, ground contact is believable, form is readable in shadowed areas. (5) Composition and polish: cart fills most of the frame with margins, cargo is neatly placed, no clipping, floating parts or z-fighting.
probe: Load the page, wait for window.__TASK_STATE__.ready === true (20s timeout), read wheelCount, spokeCount, plankCount, then capture frames at t=1s and t=3s and compute the frame difference; pass if more than 0.5% of pixels change by over 8/255 between them. Confirm canvas is non-uniform and no uncaught page errors.

title: Procedural stylised tree (seasonal)
prompt: Build a single-page browser app with the provided framework, served by vite, rendering to the canvas with id #app. Model one large, characterful stylised tree entirely from code (no external model, texture or image files), as a hero object on a small grassy mound. It must have: a thick trunk that flares into visible surface roots at the base and tapers upward, at least 3 levels of branching (trunk, major limbs, twigs) with at least 12 branches in total that fan out in different directions and taper, and a foliage crown made of at least 15 separate leaf clumps of varied size and tone (at least 3 distinct greens or autumn colours) hanging on the branch ends. Add a few details: a knot or hollow on the trunk, a small number of fallen leaves or a couple of mushrooms on the ground, and a rope swing or a bird house hanging from a limb. The branch layout must be generated by a seeded procedural routine (same seed gives the same tree). The camera frames the entire tree with sky behind and slowly orbits. Use a key light with shadows so the crown casts a shadow on the mound. After the first frame set window.__TASK_STATE__ = { ready: true, branchCount: <branches>, foliageClumpCount: <clumps>, seed: <number> }.
functionalChecklist: Page is a vite app with canvas #app rendering a non-blank 3D frame with no console errors
Source uses a seeded pseudo-random generator (not Math.random) for branch layout
Branches are generated recursively or iteratively with at least 3 levels and decreasing thickness per level
Trunk has a base flare or at least 3 visible surface roots
At least 15 foliage clumps with varied scale and at least 3 distinct colours
Detail elements exist: trunk knot/hollow, ground clutter (leaves or mushrooms), and a hanging swing or bird house
Grassy mound ground element exists and a shadow-casting key light is configured
window.__TASK_STATE__ is set after first render with ready === true, branchCount >= 12, foliageClumpCount >= 15 and a numeric seed
No external asset files are fetched
Camera orbit produces frame differences between captures 2 seconds apart
visualRubric: A strong frame shows the full tree centred with sky behind and a readable mound beneath. Score each 1-5: (1) Silhouette and organic form: trunk flare, tapering limbs and an asymmetric, believable crown rather than a lollipop of one sphere on a cylinder. (2) Detail density: multiple branching levels, varied clumps, roots, knot, swing/bird house, ground clutter all discernible. (3) Colour and material: bark and foliage are distinct, foliage has tonal variation and light/dark depth, palette is cohesive. (4) Lighting and depth: crown shadows land on the mound, light through the crown gives volume, background and ambient light avoid flatness. (5) Composition and polish: tree fits with margins, branches connect to the trunk without gaps or floating pieces, no z-fighting or clipping.
probe: Load the page, wait for window.__TASK_STATE__.ready === true (20s timeout), read branchCount, foliageClumpCount, seed; reload the page and confirm the seed and counts are identical (determinism). Capture frames at t=1s and t=3s and pass the motion check if over 0.5% of pixels differ by more than 8/255. Confirm the canvas is non-uniform and no uncaught page errors.
